Start ### Describe the bug When running `pnpm dev`, i will get the error `Could not resolve "tanstack-start-manifest:v"`. More than this, tracking down the source of this bug is terrible because any number of components breaking the server-client boundary can trigger this. Then it occurs in a way to make the development environment unstable and the error is "sticky". Here is an example I deal with. The first time this error occurs, it tracked it down to my importing the `radix-ui` library in order to use a ShadCN component [`Switch`](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/radix/switch). It look something like this: ``` import { Moon, Sun } from "lucide-react"; import { useTheme } from "next-themes"; import { useEffect, useState } from "react"; import { Switch } from "@/components/ui/switch"; export function ThemeToggle() { const [mounted, setMounted] = useState(false); const { resolvedTheme, setTheme } = useTheme(); useEffect(() => { setMounted(true); }, []); if (!mounted) { return null; } const isDark = resolvedTheme === "dark"; return (
setTheme(checked ? "dark" : "light")} aria-label="Toggle theme" />
); } ``` By removing the switch, and using a shadcn Button, the development server could start again and I didn't get the tanstack-start-injected-head-scripts:v error. But the worst part was that say this change happened at commit 10. i'm on commit 10 and the dev is breaking. So i run `git checkout commit-9`, just before it, i would still get the same dev build error. This exact reason killed a few hours because i would run `git bisect` multiple time, always choosing commit 10 as the bad commit and a commit a few times away, like commit 5 (in this example) as the good commit. I had to choose a commit very far removed, run `pnpm i`, `pnpm dev` for that previous commit to run and build successfully. If while investigating the error, git bisect went to a bad commit which caused the error, going back into time a few commits would not fix the issue, depsite running `pnpm install, build, dev ....`. This was the MOST INFURIATING THING becaues it made it difficult to pin point the true source of the error. Remove node\_modules didn't seem to help. I have to always git chekcout in a detached barnch like 10 commites back, install and build, then checkout forward again. Boils my blood thinking about this. worst thing is that I'm sure i'll get this error again and have to do this insane checkout, install, dev multipel times agian. ### Your Example Website or App N/A ### Steps to Reproduce the Bug or Issue I was not able to make a reproducible build. In my testing, setting up a blank project with `pnpm create cloudflare@latest my-tanstack-start-app --framework=tanstack-start` and then installing shadcn switch with next-themes did not trigger the same build error. Sorry ### Expected behavior The error should at least point hopefully to what might be causing the error. Or this transient build artifact file should not be lingering around. The git checkout fragility sucks. ### Screenshots or Videos [https://drive.google.com/file/d/1W5zjl3FdKVJ06lrEJojXy2N6Q3OEWaIg/view?usp=sharing](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1W5zjl3FdKVJ06lrEJojXy2N6Q3OEWaIg/view?usp=sharing) Added public google drive link. I think the issue is that the ondone handler is never called, not sure why .. but I'm about to open another bug report to get ro the root of this ;) ### CiskaLV commented on Sep 18, 2025on Sep 18, 2025 [![@CiskaLV](https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/44933905?u=a4c172ef01a7d03aca365dfa9be16d66f41de9ec&v=4&size=48)](https://github.com/CiskaLV) [CiskaLV](https://github.com/CiskaLV) [on Sep 18, 2025on Sep 18, 2025](https://github.com/TanStack/router/issues/5065#issuecomment-3309525848) Last edited by CiskaLV More actions Ye I tried to check and the onDone is never called same with the onError im using everything latest 1.131.47 for router and start and @tanstack/solid-query 5.89.0 Edit: When i first setup the example it had @tanstack/solid-start@1.121.3 and that worked with out any errors and actually loaded ### Dillpickleschmidt commented on Sep 30, 2025on Sep 30, 2025 [![@Dillpickleschmidt](https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/36453037?v=4&size=48)](https://github.com/Dillpickleschmidt) [Dillpickleschmidt](https://github.com/Dillpickleschmidt) [on Sep 30, 2025on Sep 30, 2025](https://github.com/TanStack/router/issues/5065#issuecomment-3354136976) Last edited by Dillpickleschmidt More actions ## Workaround: Custom Hook Using QueryObserver So you don't spend 24 hours banging your head against a wall with this issue (like I did), here's a working solution. Something about TanStack Query's `useQuery` doesn't signal SSR completion properly. You can work around this by creating a custom hook that uses `useQuery`'s internal `QueryObserver` on the server, and the original `useQuery` on the client: ``` export function useCustomQuery( options: () => SolidQueryOptions, ): UseQueryResult { const queryClient = useQueryClient() return createIsomorphicFn() .server(function (queryClient: QueryClient, options) { const resolvedOptions = options() const observer = new QueryObserver(queryClient, resolvedOptions) // Check if data is already available synchronously const cachedData = queryClient.getQueryData(resolvedOptions.queryKey) const hasCachedData = cachedData !== undefined // Only use createResource if data is not cached (for Suspense integration) const [data] = hasCachedData ? [() => cachedData as TData] : createResource(() => queryClient.ensureQueryData(resolvedOptions)) // Proxy to get fresh snapshot on every property access return new Proxy({} as UseQueryResult, { get(_target, prop) { const result = observer.getOptimisticResult(resolvedOptions) if (prop === "data") { // If observer has placeholderData, use it (avoid Suspense) if (result.data !== undefined) { return result.data } // Otherwise use resource (triggers Suspense if pending) return data() } return result[prop as keyof typeof result] }, }) }) .client(function (_queryClient: QueryClient, options) { return useQuery(options) })(queryClient, options) as UseQueryResult } ``` EDIT 10/2: updated to make `options` a function to keep it reactive to changes **Important:** If you're deferring queries from the server without awaiting them (i.e. with `prefetchQuery`), configure your router to dehydrate pending queries (idk why `shouldDehydrateQuery` isn't in the docs but you'll need it to stream queries that are still pending--i.e. requested but not resolved before the page is sent): ``` // router.tsx const router = createTanStackRouter({ routeTree, context: { queryClient }, dehydrate: () => ({ queryClientState: dehydrate(queryClient, { shouldDehydrateQuery: () => true, // Include all queries (even pending) }), }), hydrate: (dehydrated) => { hydrate(queryClient, dehydrated.queryClientState) }, }) ``` **Usage:** ``` // Route loader - prefetch without awaiting loader: ({ context }) => { context.queryClient.prefetchQuery(myQueryOptions) } // Component - use like normal useQuery function MyComponent() { const query = useCustomQuery(() => myQueryOptions) return
{query.data}
} ``` This gives you: - ✅ No hanging spinner - ✅ Single fetch (server-initiated, client-hydrated) - ✅ Full cache reactivity - ✅ Identical API to `useQuery` - ✅ Suspense works fine with the createResource that we added to the hook ourselves. The server uses the same `QueryObserver.getOptimisticResult()` that `useQuery` uses internally. Edit: I'm not expert in any of this but it seems to work from my initial testing. Due to being unfamiliar with the inner-workings of TanStack Query and not thoroughly testing beyond my own needs, I may be neglecting some edge cases. YMMV. ### Dillpickleschmidt commented on Sep 30, 2025on Sep 30, 2025 [![@Dillpickleschmidt](https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/36453037?v=4&size=48)](https://github.com/Dillpickleschmidt) [Dillpickleschmidt](https://github.com/Dillpickleschmidt) [on Sep 30, 2025on Sep 30, 2025](https://github.com/TanStack/router/issues/5065#issuecomment-3354358755) Last edited by Dillpickleschmidt More actions Here's a test I ran that you can try yourself to confirm that deferred loading is working. It tests 3 things, an instant response in the server, a fast response (100ms), and a slow response (10s). This should ensure that you get the first 2 responses in the initial HTML from the server, and that the slow response streams in from the initial request. ### Describe the bug

### Describe the bug

In a TanStack Start app using Vite 8, the root route imports global CSS via `import stylesUrl from '../styles.css?url'` and passes `stylesUrl` to `createRootRoute().head().links` as `href`.

After `vite build`, **the client bundle** emits one hashed CSS file under `dist/client/assets/` (e.g. `styles-AAAA.css`), while the **SSR bundle** resolves `?url` to a **different** path (e.g. `/assets/styles-BBBB.css`) baked into `dist/server/assets/router-*.js`. The file `styles-BBBB.css` exists under `dist/server/assets/` but **not** under `dist/client/assets/`.

If the production server only serves static files from `dist/client` (common for TanStack Start + custom Bun/Node servers), the browser requests `/assets/styles-BBBB.css` from the HTML shell → **404**. The client entry then loads the correct CSS from the client graph → page recovers after a second request.

This shows up reliably for us when building **inside Linux/Docker (Alpine)**; copying a `dist/` produced on macOS into the same server layout works in our tests, so the mismatch is tied to **where `vite build` runs**, not mixed deploy artifacts.

### Reproduction

1. TanStack Start + `@tanstack/react-router` root route:

   - `import appCss from '../styles.css?url'`
   - `head: () => ({ links: [{ rel: 'stylesheet', href: appCss }] })`
2. Run `vite build` (or `bun run build`) **on Linux** (e.g. `oven/bun:alpine` Docker image).
3. Inspect:
   - `dist/client/assets/styles-*.css` (hashes + file sizes)
   - `dist/server/assets/styles-*.css`
   - `dist/server/assets/router-*.js` for `var … = "/assets/styles-….css"`
4. Confirm SSR `href` uses a filename that **does not** exist under `dist/client/assets/`.

I can provide a minimal public repo if needed.

### Expected behavior

The URL embedded in the SSR bundle for `*.css?url` should refer to the **same** emitted asset as the client build (same basename under `/assets/`), **or** the framework docs should clearly state that production must also serve `dist/server/assets` for CSS emitted only on the SSR graph.

If this is intentional, guidance on `build.ssrEmitAssets` / recommended pattern for global CSS in Start would help.

### Actual behavior

- Client: `dist/client/assets/styles-<HashA>.css`
- SSR router chunk: `href` → `/assets/styles-<HashB>.css`
- `dist/server/assets/styles-<HashB>.css` exists; `dist/client/assets/styles-<HashB>.css` does not → 404 when only `dist/client` is exposed.

### System Info

- Vite: 8.x
- `@tanstack/react-start`: 1.16x
- OS (build): Linux Alpine (Docker) vs macOS (local)
- Node/Bun: (fill in)

### Additional context

- `build.ssrEmitAssets: true` was tried; behavior may still leave SSR and client CSS hashes diverging depending on pipeline.
- Workaround we are considering: drop `?url` and use side-effect `import '../styles.css'`, **or** merge `dist/server/assets` into static routes for `/assets/*`.

### Evidence (from one build output)

dist/client/assets/styles-CAcMLtju.css # present

dist/server/assets/styles-CvozrKM9.css # present (different hash/size)

router-\*.js contains: "/assets/styles-CvozrKM9.css"

However, after running the full Docker build process, I encounter a CSS 404 error, and then I need to restore it.

Thank you.

WORKDIR /app

ENV CI=1

The output from the same image build within the `app/` directory copied from Docker is sufficient to illustrate the problem, leading to the following conclusions:

1. Inconsistent CSS filenames (directly corresponding to browser issues)


Location Files

`app/dist/client/assets/styles-CAcMLtju.css` (approx. 72KB)

`app/dist/server/assets/styles-CvozrKM9.css` (approx. 97KB)

In other words, the client and SSR each produced CSS files with different hashes and sizes (this is not a case of "missing files copied," but rather Vite's interpretation of the same `styles.css` is inconsistent across the client and SSR pipelines).

The `server.ts` file only scans `dist/client` for static resources. Therefore, `/assets/styles-CAcMLtju.css` is found, but `/assets/styles-CvozrKM9.css` does not exist in the `client` directory → initially resulting in a 404 error; then the client fetches `CAcMLtju` according to its own chunks, and the page is restored.

2. The SSR hardcodes the file that's "not present in the client," but is present in `app/dist/server/assets/router-C1PLAuD7.js`:

`router-C1PLAuD7.js`

Lines 27-27

`var styles_default = "/assets/styles-CvozrKM9.css";`

This is consistent with your `import '../styles.css?url' + head.links` in `__root.tsx`: `?url` is parsed as `CvozrKM9` in the SSR bundle, while the browser should actually use `CAcMLtju` from the client.

3. Relationship with Dockerfile


From `app/`, we can confirm that the vite build running in the container is itself a "self-consistent error": the same build generates two CSS versions simultaneously.

The root cause is that the static strategy of styles.css?url + only serving dist/client is more easily exposed on Linux/Docker; it is not a simple Dockerfile error such as "dist was not copied" or "two builds were mixed up".

### Which project does this relate to?

Start

### Describe the bug

Hi, in a TanStack Start project, when I am updating code during development triggers a hydration failure. While the change is reflected immediately via Hot Module Replacement, a subsequent manual browser reload results in a "Hydration failed" error. The issue persists until the dev server is stopped and restarted.

### Your Example Website or App

[https://github.com/Alan-aj/tanstack-start](https://github.com/Alan-aj/tanstack-start)

### Steps to Reproduce the Bug or Issue

1. Initialize a project using the TanStack Start Starter Template.
2. Run the development server.
3. Modify a component (e.g., change text) and save.
4. Observe the change reflecting in the browser via HMR.
5. Manually reload the browser page.
6. Check the console for the following error

`Uncaught Error: Hydration failed because the server rendered HTML didn't match the client. As a result this tree will be regenerated on the client. This can happen if a SSR-ed Client Component used: ...`

Should reload without errors

Issue body actions

### Which project does this relate to?

Start

### Describe the bug

In `headContentUtils.tsx`, `preloadLinks` are placed **before**`links`, which means `<link rel="modulepreload">` elements appear before `<link rel="stylesheet">` in the rendered `<head>`.

Browsers fetch resources top-to-bottom. When modulepreload links come first, the render-blocking CSS resources needed to display styled SSR HTML get discovered late. Under HTTP/1.1's [6-connection-per-host limit](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/network/reference#timing-explanation), the CSS request can't even start until earlier JS downloads free up a connection.

Key result (Using a slow 4G throttle + 22 slow modulepreload links):

| Scenario | FCP | Δ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| HTTP/1.1 — modulepreload first | 2075ms |  |
| HTTP/1.1 — stylesheet first | 1260ms | **−815ms (39%)** |
| HTTP/2 — modulepreload first | 1388ms |  |
| HTTP/2 — stylesheet first | 1380ms | **−8ms (~1%)** |

ℹ️ Happy to open a PR if this is something you'd like to see fixed. 🚀

### Your Example Website or App

[https://github.com/steschi/html-head-order-matters](https://github.com/steschi/html-head-order-matters)

### Steps to Reproduce the Bug or Issue

1. Create a TanStack Router SSR app with multiple route chunks (so Vite emits many modulepreload links) as well as a stylesheet import.
2. Build and serve with `vite preview` (HTTP/1.1)
3. Open Chrome DevTools → Network tab, throttle to Slow 4G
4. Load the page and observe the waterfall: modulepreload fetches start before the stylesheet fetch
5. The stylesheet is blocked behind the 6-connection limit, delaying FCP

### Expected behavior

`<link rel="stylesheet">` should appear **before**`<link rel="modulepreload">` in the `<head>`, so the browser discovers and fetches render-blocking CSS first. This matches the [capo.js](https://github.com/rviscomi/capo.js) recommended element ordering (stylesheets = weight 5, modulepreload = weight 4).

### Screenshots or Videos

See the full reproduction repo for waterfall charts and Chrome DevTools traces:

[https://github.com/steschi/html-head-order-matters](https://github.com/steschi/html-head-order-matters)

![Inefficient head order](https://private-user-images.githubusercontent.com/8997333/553819133-70f13e76-b299-46bc-b1f0-cf58c81d2101.png?jwt=eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1QiLCJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9..BZESFeNvqN60GwqP_x0VHSBLOPPHfho3nvjVn2mLJKo)  ![Performant head order](https://private-user-images.githubusercontent.com/8997333/553819399-31083795-d45f-4dbc-b1e3-d75f6af30403.png?jwt=eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1QiLCJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9..uGBz3GOnuZF9THK1Cfup4arE_LvLrUggz6EEVh5UltY)

### Platform

- Router / Start Version: 1.162.4 with nitro v3
- OS: macOS
- Browser: Chrome
- Browser Version: Chrome 145

### Additional context

- [capo.js](https://github.com/rviscomi/capo.js) — `<head>` ordering audit tool by Rick Viscomi (Google)
- [Harry Roberts — "Get Your Head Straight"](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uqLl-Yew2o8) — talk on `<head>` ordering and Core Web Vitals

Issue body actions

> **Re-occurrence of [#5673](https://github.com/TanStack/router/issues/5673)** — same error string, same source position (`default-entry/server.ts:8:15`). Filing as a new issue per [@schiller-manuel](https://github.com/schiller-manuel)'s request in [#5673](https://github.com/TanStack/router/issues/5673) ("please create a new issue including a complete reproducer project"). The original issue was closed, but the failure is still present on the latest `@tanstack/react-start` (1.167.50, 22 minor versions past [@zotodev](https://github.com/zotodev)'s regression report at 1.145.10).

## Summary

Every SSR HMR pass throws `(0, __vite_ssr_import_0__.createStartHandler) is not a function` on `@tanstack/react-start@1.167.50`. Cold start always succeeds; the second-and-subsequent SSR pass after Vite invalidates the module graph fails. The dev server becomes unusable as soon as anything is edited until it's killed and restarted.

Identical to [@Flusinerd](https://github.com/Flusinerd)'s report in [#5673](https://github.com/TanStack/router/issues/5673) against Nitro — same error string at the same source position — so the bug isn't specific to any one SSR runner; this report adds Cloudflare workerd (`@cloudflare/vite-plugin`) to the list of affected runners.

## Reproduction

1. Boot `vite dev`. First request to `/` returns 200.
2. `touch src/lib/seo/meta.ts` (any source edit, including a one-character `styles.css` change).
3. Next request returns 500 with the stack above. 100% reproducible.

## Root cause analysis

`createStartHandler` is exported through a two-level wildcard re-export chain:

- `@tanstack/react-start/server` (`dist/esm/server.js`) → `export * from "@tanstack/react-start-server"`
- `@tanstack/react-start-server@1.166.44` (`dist/esm/index.js`) → `export * from "@tanstack/start-server-core"; export { StartServer, defaultRenderHandler, defaultStreamHandler };`
- `@tanstack/start-server-core@1.167.22` — direct named export of `createStartHandler`.

Vite's SSR transform compiles `export * from '...'` into a runtime call that copies enumerable own properties from the imported namespace into the current module's namespace at evaluation time. When the worker entry is invalidated by HMR and the runner re-evaluates the chain, the deeply-nested wildcard re-exports do not consistently rebind `createStartHandler` onto the outermost namespace — the static top-level binding `__vite_ssr_import_0__.createStartHandler` resolves to `undefined`.

This matches [@Flusinerd](https://github.com/Flusinerd)'s repro on Nitro (`nitro/dist/runtime/internal/vite/dev-worker.mjs`, identical error string at the same `default-entry/server.ts:8:15` source position), so the bug appears to be in the re-export chain itself, not in any individual SSR runner.

## Workaround that worked

Replacing the auto-generated `@tanstack/react-start/server-entry` with a user-owned entry that defers the import to runtime:

```
// src/server.ts
let cachedFetch:
  | ((req: Request, env: unknown, ctx: unknown) => Promise<Response>)
  | null = null

async function getFetch() {
  if (cachedFetch) return cachedFetch
  const mod = await import('@tanstack/react-start/server')
  cachedFetch = mod.createStartHandler(mod.defaultStreamHandler) as (
    req: Request,
    env: unknown,
    ctx: unknown
  ) => Promise<Response>
  return cachedFetch
}

if (import.meta.hot) {
  import.meta.hot.accept(() => {
    cachedFetch = null
  })
}

export default {
  async fetch(request: Request, env: unknown, ctx: unknown) {
    const fn = await getFetch()
    return await fn(request, env, ctx)
  }
}
```

```
// wrangler.jsonc
"main": "./src/server.ts"  // was "@tanstack/react-start/server-entry"
```

Verified across 10 HMR cycles + a Playwright-driven page load — zero recurrences. The dynamic `await import(...)` (resolved through `__vite_ssr_dynamic_import__`) materializes the namespace at call time, by which point the inner chain has finished re-evaluating, and the wildcard re-exports are complete. Static top-level destructuring is what trips the bug; deferring to a runtime call avoids it.

## What didn't work

- **Clearing `node_modules/.vite/`** — repro on the very first HMR after a fresh boot.
- **Custom `src/server.ts` with the same static top-level import from `@tanstack/react-start/server`** — same chain, same error, just relocated to user source.
- **Direct deep imports** of `createStartHandler` from `@tanstack/start-server-core` and `defaultStreamHandler` from `@tanstack/react-start-server` (declared as direct deps to bypass the wildcard) — fails because `start-server-core` references plugin-provided virtual specifiers (`#tanstack-start-entry`, `#tanstack-start-plugin-adapters`, `tanstack-start-manifest:v`, `tanstack-start-injected-head-scripts:v`) that the `tanstackStart` Vite plugin only resolves when the import path flows through the official `@tanstack/react-start` package facade. esbuild errors out with `Could not resolve "#tanstack-start-entry"`.
- **Downgrading** — [@ulrichstark](https://github.com/ulrichstark)'s bisect in [ReferenceError: Cannot access '\_\_vite\_ssr\_import\_2\_\_' before initialization #5673](https://github.com/TanStack/router/issues/5673) found 1.142.1 fixed the original report, but [@zotodev](https://github.com/zotodev) confirmed regression at 1.145.10, and we're 22 minor versions past that.

### Which project does this relate to?

### Describe the bug

I'm out of town this weekend but was running into this so wanted to file this bug report sooner than later.

I'm using alchemy, which wraps `cloudflare-vite` to run tanstack start. I haven't had time to create a clean reproduction but basically what seems to be happening, is that my auth service is created as an `Effect.Service` from `effect-ts`. One of the other deps coming is is my Drizzle postgres client from `'@effect/sql-drizzle/Pg'`.

As soon as i import `import { auth } from '@repo/core/auth/handler'` into `server.ts` or `routes/api/auth/$.ts` my app blows up with the error below. `handler.ts` imports my Runtime from effect, which has all my app dependencies, which some are required for some of the `hooks` that better auth calls in the Effectful Better Auth instance.

Possibly related to [vitejs/vite#20867 (comment)](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/issues/20867#issuecomment-3431250189). I was seeing pre-bundling issues on later versions of vite.

The web app producing this error is a basic `better-t-stack` templated start app, with the only changes adding in alchemy and dropping in my auth into the server route. Everything starts up fine without the eventual better-auth dependency as described above.
